statement: Whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns a result r, there exists an integer q with q >= 0 such that S(nums) = q * M + r and 0 <= r < M. Equivalently, r is the unique canonical residue S(nums) mod M, namely the remainder of the total sum over all ordered pairs (i,j), including i=j, after division by M.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007. Define S(nums) = sum over all ordered index pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n of floor(nums[i] / nums[j]), where floor is ordinary integer division of positive integers; the diagonal pairs i=j are included.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns some result r. It does not fail by arithmetic overflow, division by zero, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, r is a nonnegative integer strictly less than M, and moreover r <= S(nums). Thus the returned value is never negative, never reaches M, and never exceeds the true unmodded sum.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007 and let S(nums) be the unmodded ordered-pair total defined in spec_1.

statement: Let nums' be any slice that is a permutation of nums: len(nums') = n and there is a bijection pi on the indices {0,...,n-1} such that nums'[i] = nums[pi(i)] for every i. If sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r and sum_of_floored_pairs(nums') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let k >= 1 be an integer and let nums' be a slice with len(nums') = n such that nums'[i] = k * nums[i] for every i and 1 <= nums'[i] <= 100000 for every i. If sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r and sum_of_floored_pairs(nums') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: If S(nums) < M, then whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, r = S(nums). In particular, under this condition r >= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007 and let S(nums) be the unmodded ordered-pair total defined in spec_1.

statement: If S(nums) >= M, then whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, there is an integer q with q >= 1 such that S(nums) = q * M + r and 0 <= r < M. Equivalently, r is the remainder after subtracting floor(S(nums) / M) copies of M from S(nums).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007 and let S(nums) be the unmodded ordered-pair total defined in spec_1.

statement: Whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, r is congruent modulo M to n + T(nums), where T(nums) = sum over ordered pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i,j < n and i != j of floor(nums[i] / nums[j]). That is, r is congruent modulo M to the diagonal contribution n plus the off-diagonal ordered-pair total.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007.

statement: Whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, r is congruent modulo M to n + sum over ordered pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i,j < n, i != j, and nums[i] >= nums[j] of floor(nums[i] / nums[j]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007.

statement: Let V be the set of distinct values appearing in nums, and for each v in V let c(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = v. Whenever sum_of_floored_pairs(nums) returns r, r is congruent modulo M to the sum over all u in V and all v in V of c(u) * c(v) * floor(u / v).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Let M = 1000000007.
